To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified the four CatSper genes in the bovines genome, profiled their mRNA expression along the reproductive tract and confirmed their expression in bull testicular tissues, and that we identified CatSper channels on bull sperm.
We identified the CATSPPER1 protein in the bovine and demonstrated that it is involved in the hyperactivation and rheo-tactic response of bull sperm.
CatSper channels are present in bull sperm and mediate calcium influx that is required for hyperactivation and the sperm’s rheotactic response to flow in the female reproductive tract.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of calcium influx via CatSper calcium channels in sperm function in the reproductive tract.
the molecular basis of sperm function.
the identification, expression and function of CATSPER genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CatSper channels are present in the sperm and are responsible for the hyperactivation and rheo-tactic responses.
the calcium influx in bull sperm occurs through CatSper channels, as it has been shown in other species.

blocking the calcium channel in sperm using ethylene glycol tetracetic acid, mibefradil or CATSPER antibody significantly inhibited caffeine induced hyperactivation and rheotropic response, suggesting that CatSper channels are involved in sperm motility and rheotaxis in bovine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified the CatSper channel genes in the bovines and profiled their mRNA expression in reproductive tissue and have demonstrated that the CatSper channels are involved in the regulation of bull sperm function.
CatSper channels are conserved in the bovine and that they are expressed in testicular tissue.

we identified all four CatSper genes in the bovin genome, profiled their expression in testicular tissue and along the reproductive tract, and showed that blocking CatSper channels inhibits sperm motility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CatSper channels are present on the sperm in the bull and they play a critical role in sperm motility and hyperactivation.

the calcium channels in bull sperm are similar to those in humans, and that blocking the channels with a calcium chelator or a specific antibody inhibits sperm hyperactivation and rheotropic response.
CatSper channels are expressed in bull sperm and that blocking the calcium influx via these channels can inhibit sperm function.
